goal: Give agent-kit pstack's comment discipline in two forms, as Beau asked on 2026-11-21: the /no-comments skill with its comment-sicko subagent, and a mechanical check that catches a comment a diff adds.
changed: New no-comments skill and comment-sicko agent in bstack, adapted from pstack. The keep-list lives once, in a snippet both of them inline.
comments.py lists the comments a diff adds to Python files and exits 1 when there is one. A moved comment adds nothing; a shebang, a tool directive, a license header and a linked comment pass.
agent-kit's reliability checklist gains added-comment, which runs comments.py on every change to a Python file.
beau-mode's comment rule now points at the keep-list, which no longer allows a comment that explains a surprise in our own code. Opening a PR runs no-comments when the diff adds comments.

claims.claim: comments.py lists exactly the comments a diff adds to Python files, applies its four keeps, and exits 0, 1 or 2 as documented.
claims.check: tests/test_comments.py, 28 tests on throwaway git repos, on Python 3.12 and 3.9.6; four mutations of the script each fail a test; make unit
claims.remaining: Python only. Files in other languages are not read.

claims.claim: The check runs on real history without an error, and fails where comments were added.
claims.check: comments.py --base C^ --head C over the 156 non-merge commits on main: 60 exit 1, 96 exit 0, none exit 2
claims.remaining: Nobody read the 60 to count how many of their comments the keep-list would allow with a link added.

claims.claim: bstack installs from this checkout and a Claude Code session lists the no-comments skill and the comment-sicko agent.
claims.check: verify-kit drive all, 4 of 4 features, with the real claude CLI in a throwaway profile, reading the agent and skill lists from the session's init line; make claude-validate
claims.remaining: Claude Code only: no other tool was tried.

claims.claim: An agent following the skill deletes narration, dead code and unproven notes, keeps a license header and a proven external constraint, fixes the code a comment covered for, and leaves the check at exit 0.
claims.check: Two runs on a scratch repo seeded with one comment of each kind, each an opus agent following SKILL.md with a sonnet hunter: one on the first draft, one on the rewritten text. Both did all of the above. I read each diff and reran the check
claims.remaining: The second run deleted a module docstring, and the sentence that now forbids that has not been tried. Both runs were one model family on one seeded repo, and the agent knew it was reading a skill from disk. No Eval playbook comparison ran.

claims.claim: The skill loads when a user types one of the phrases in its description.
claims.remaining: The skill-description checklist item asks for each phrase typed in a session with the plugin installed. None was typed.

next.item: Sweep the 385 comment lines already in the kit's Python with /no-comments
next.source: inferred: the check only judges what a diff adds, and 60 of 156 past commits would fail it
next.why_now: Any edit near an old comment now meets the rule, so the old ones cost a little on every change until they go.
next.impact: Whoever next edits quality.py (128 comment lines) stops tripping the check on text they did not write.

next.item: Try the fixed skill text with the Eval playbook, on a second model family
next.why_now: Opening a PR now calls the skill, so every code change in a repo that uses beau-mode will run it.
next.impact: Beau learns whether agents delete too much or too little before the rule runs on real PRs.

next.item: A rule for TypeScript, in the project's own linter
next.why_now: Not yet: wait for the first TypeScript repo that adopts the skill.
next.impact: Until then the skill's judgment is the only check on comments outside Python.
